A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study. Their main texts, figures, tables and complete appendices are readable, and retained content can be matched across renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original perturbation evaluations, consistency analyses and controlled RL finetuning experiments in Sections 2–3 and the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and adds closed-model comparisons, control experiments, grounding evaluations and a human annotation study.

M1.justification: The GRPO training, rewards, augmentation probabilities and consistency judge are retained. Appendix C.4 adds a procedural adaptation of perturbation construction: misleading directions are derived by reversing the gold bounding box's spatial direction, instead of selecting an incorrect answer option.

E1.justification: v3 retains the original spatial/general-VQA benchmarks and training datasets, but adds RefCOCOg referring-expression localization, extending evaluation to bounding-box prediction. Appendix C.1 also adds evaluation scenarios with correct auxiliary text and uninformative captions.

E2.justification: The original Qwen-based comparison suite is retained. v3 adds o3, o4-mini, Gemini-2.5-Pro and Gemini-3.1-Pro Preview to the main Wrong-Caption/Wrong-Think comparisons, and evaluates InternVL3-8B and SenseNova-SI in Appendix C.3.

E3.justification: New protocols include grounding metrics, caption/thinking controls and a 600-example human study with three ratings per example. Closed-model Wrong-Think requests prefix copying rather than forcing continuation, and accuracy excludes answerless generations (Section 2.2). Existing GRPO settings in Table 7 remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix C.1 tests whether failures reflect misleading semantics rather than extra prompt text. New analyses examine model-family generalization, directional localization errors and human validation of the judge (C.3–C.6). Appendix E adds closed-model conflict-resolution and hallucination cases. Earlier abstention and reward analyses remain.

E5.justification: v1 already reports across-dataset standard deviations and inter-judge kappa statistics. v3 extends reliability estimation to human annotations, including Krippendorff's alpha and agreement against human majority labels (Tables 11–14). It does not add explicit RL run counts or confidence intervals; the seed-variability caveat is retained.

E6.justification: Existing values in Tables 1, 2, 6 and 8 are unchanged, but substantial new results are added. On newly evaluated RefCOCOg, SpaceR has relative mean-IoU drops of 39% under Wrong-Caption and 80% under Wrong-Think (Table 10). Human–Qwen3 agreement is 91.8%, with kappa 0.813 (Table 13). New plots report closed models, controls and InternVL variants.

T1.justification: Appendix C.4 introduces a quantitative definition of directional follow rate: the fraction of examples whose perturbed predicted box center shifts toward the injected direction relative to its default prediction. This is a limited new metric definition; no theorem, proof or substantial theoretical framework is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion add a headline claim that closed models show stronger robustness and reasoning consistency, interpreting the gap as an underdeveloped capability of open models rather than an inherent task limitation. The original accuracy–consistency tradeoff and augmentation/reward conclusions remain.

C2.justification: v3 explicitly distinguishes answer–reasoning consistency from internal causal faithfulness. It adds interpretations of semantic versus formatting effects, conservative judge bias relative to humans, and closed-model conflict resolution. Appendix C.4 also limits the grounding experiment to a proof of concept rather than a full grounding-faithfulness evaluation.

D1.justification: v3 adds exact closed-model prompt templates, examples explaining augmentation of the existing general-VQA datasets, grounding perturbation instructions and human sampling/labeling details. The original training hyperparameters, augmentation-generation prompt and consistency-judge prompt are retained.

R1.justification: Related work adds discussion of VLM-R3, CertainlyUncertain and Parcalabescu and Frank, while the introduction cites Jacovi and Goldberg to distinguish faithfulness concepts. Sources for the new models and grounding dataset are added. The overall positioning as a diagnostic study of RL-with-CoT remains.

P1.justification: v3 separates open- and closed-model evaluation, adds an appendix contents page, clarifies terminology and rewrites the conclusion. Most existing prose and the main section sequence remain intact; the expansion does not constitute a wholesale narrative reorganization.

P2.justification: The main perturbation plots are redrawn to include closed models and revised legends. New control, consistency and InternVL plots, grounding/human-study tables and illustrated traces substantially expand the displays. Older figures are largely retained and relocated. Figure 3 introduces a caption that reverses the open/closed line styles shown in its legend.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially strengthens the study's validity: semantic controls address a prompt-format confound, human annotations independently validate the automated consistency judge, and another model family plus localization test generality. Explicitly limiting faithfulness to consistency also reduces interpretive ambiguity. Different prefix control and answer filtering limit the new open/closed comparison, but these caveats and minor presentation errors do not outweigh the stronger support for the central findings.
